quiz.q: How did cultural nationalist Aurobindo Ghosh differ from early nationalists like Surendranath Banerjee regarding Indian nationhood?
options: Ghosh argued India was a nation from the beginning, while Banerjee considered it a nation in making.
Ghosh dismissed the concept of nationhood, while Banerjee believed British rule created Indian national unity.
Ghosh defined nationhood through class struggle, while Banerjee rooted it in ancient religious revivalism.
Ghosh saw India as an artificial construct, while Banerjee regarded it as merely a geographical expression.
quiz.why: Aurobindo Ghosh rejected the early nationalist view of India as a nation in making, asserting that India was a nation from the beginning.

quiz.q: How did Bipin Chandra's Marxist assessment of the Indian National Movement differ from orthodox Marxist interpretations?
options: He dismissed the national movement as elite factional rivalry orchestrated entirely by community power brokers.
He maintained it was a spectacular mass movement rather than simply an instrument of the bourgeoisie.
He characterized the struggle as a reactionary feudal uprising aimed at restoring pre-colonial monarchies.
He rejected the movement as a conscious bourgeois conspiracy organized against the Indian laboring masses.
quiz.why: Unlike orthodox Marxists who dismissed Congress as purely bourgeois, Bipin Chandra argued it led a spectacular mass national movement.

quiz.q: On what primary ground did B.R. Ambedkar critique the Congress-led movement and reject Indian nationhood?
options: He opposed industrial modernization and demanded a return to self-sufficient agrarian village republics.
He advocated an immediate armed revolution rather than constitutional negotiations with the colonial government.
He argued that genuine nationhood requires social fraternity, which cannot exist alongside pervasive caste oppression.
He sought complete integration into Congress provided Dalit representatives received permanent executive veto power.
quiz.why: Ambedkar maintained that true nationhood is founded on social fraternity, which is impossible without first eradicating caste oppression.

quiz.q: According to M.N. Roy's Radical Humanist philosophy, why was conventional nationalism fundamentally flawed?
options: It failed to establish a strong centralized state capable of directing socialist production.
It focused exclusively on cultural revivalism while neglecting the necessity of constitutional reforms.
It compromised too readily with colonial rulers instead of demanding complete economic autarky.
It suppressed individual freedom, whereas humanity needed a cosmopolitan union of liberated individuals.
quiz.why: M.N. Roy argued that nationalism suppresses the individual, proposing instead a cosmopolitan union of liberated human beings.
